leads.summary: An identityless real internal connector can disappear from the Display panel while it has no EDID and no modes
leads.consequence: This predicate tests state, not whether an internal connector is a duplicate. A connected physical eDP/LVDS/DSI panel with an unreadable EDID and zero modes is removed from line 7, even when it is the sole internal output; line 1 and laptop helper still report it. If there is only one other display, Panel.qml:75-81,793-820 suppresses the entire DISPLAYS section, preventing the panel from offering that real internal output until metadata/modes return. The upstream source establishes the output shape, not its frequency on particular hardware; no physical session was queried.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus S15 (hypothesis); design tradeoff, not published

leads.summary: The new frontend test proves the opposite of the PR description, and passes with unchanged production code
leads.consequence: The PR description says parseDisplays drops an enabled 0x0 and thereby excludes it from the enabled count. It does not: the newly added test expects that 0x0 entry to remain, with enabledDisplayCount=2. Both the changed test and the entire original Model.js pass when run against the pinned merge-base and the current quattro tip. The safety count is now based on the backend-filtered list only; a modeless external stays enabled and counted as an independently enabled display. Clarify the description and make the test exercise the backend-to-frontend boundary rather than suggesting a nonexistent frontend filter.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (stale parseDisplays description); published as finding 1

leads.summary: The changed tests cannot catch the backend accidentally dropping a user-disabled HDMI output
leads.consequence: The only disabled HDMI-A-1 record is handed directly to parseDisplays by a preexisting JS test; none of the backend fixtures sends a disabled external through omarchy-monitor-state. A plausible mutant that filters disabled external outputs while retaining disabled internal panels passes both changed test files. That mutant would remove the user-disabled HDMI from the panel, leaving no way to turn it back on there. Add an identity-bearing disabled external fixture (and ideally an identityless disabled external as a separate case) through monitor_state and assert line 7 retains it.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator: sealed mutant run statuses 0/0, no disabled external fixture in head monitor-state-test.sh; Opus re-ran in self-check (run 3); published in Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Related open Display-panel PRs collide on the exact per-display projection and tests
leads.consequence: #12683, #13293, #11855, #12439, #10194 and #7493 are diverged open PRs editing the same list expression (not stacked). #13293/#11855 need scale; #10194 needs scale,x,y; #7493 needs transform; #12439 needs refreshRate. A merge that resolves the hunk in favor of #12072 silently removes these fields from those PRs' panel features. A merge retaining scale makes #12072's exact JSON assertions fail until its test fixtures/expected arrays are updated. #12683's alternative internal filter also conflicts at this hunk. Combine the filter with the union of projection fields and reconcile exact JSON assertions when integrating these branches. This is an integration warning about two as-yet-unmerged PRs, not a defect of #12072 alone.
leads.triage: factual, verified: conflict markers in merges with #12683/#13293/#11855, PR states open, #13293 adds scale to projection; Opus confirmed in self-check; published as Related open PRs note (JSON-assertion breakage claim not published)

leads.summary: The separate ghost-disabling PR does not stop the reload loop when the real panel is clamshelled
leads.consequence: #10198, also copied into draft #12683, disables a ghost only if another internal output is enabled with a nonzero mode. The exact new `lid_behind_ghost` fixture in #12072 has the real panel disabled and the ghost enabled at 0x0. On that state #10198's helper returns without disabling the ghost, and the existing watcher keeps treating it as modeless and repeatedly reloading at up-to-60-second intervals. This PR only hides the row, and does not stop that background loop. No new regression, but do not assume #10198 plus this PR fully repairs the closed-lid case; a hardware/runtime check could establish whether the ghost persists after a real clamshell disable.
leads.triage: factual, verified in pr-10198.diff predicate; concerns #10198 not this PR; kept in REPORT.md only

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

No correctness defect found in the tested scope. The main suggestions are to bring the PR description up to date with the head and to describe the `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-laptop` change.

**Verified** at head `c03578cf`, on Hyprland-shaped test inputs:

- An internal connector (`eDP`/`LVDS`/`DSI`) that is 0×0, has no modes and has an empty description, make and model is dropped from the Display panel list (line 7 of `omarchy-monitor-state`), whichever eDP number it has and whether it is enabled or disabled.
- A clamshelled internal panel, a disabled external and an enabled external that has not reported a mode yet all stay in the list.
- The field assumptions match Hyprland 0.56.2 source: an enabled output with no modes keeps `disabled: false` at 0×0, `description` is built from make, model and serial, and `availableModes` is filled at connect time whether or not the output is enabled.
- `monitor-state-test.sh`, `monitor-test.sh` and the related monitor tests pass at head and with the four changed files applied to the current `quattro` tip. The new state and laptop tests fail against the pre-PR scripts.

### The description predates the last commit

The description says "`parseDisplays` also drops an enabled 0×0, so a live ghost cannot count as a second screen or let you disable the last real output." Commit `1c5764a2` added that filter to `Model.js`, but `c03578cf` removed it, and `Model.js` is not in the net diff. The new `monitor-test.sh` case asserts the opposite: `parseDisplays` keeps an enabled 0×0 `DP-1` and counts two enabled displays.

Other parts of the description that no longer match:

- "`omarchy-monitor-state` omits a connector that has no geometry, no modes, and no identity": at head only internal-named connectors are omitted. Externals in that state are kept on purpose.
- The Tests paragraph: `monitor-test.sh` no longer covers a ghost, and no new or changed test sends a user-disabled HDMI through `omarchy-monitor-state`. The `lone_ghost` and laptop-helper tests, and the modeless-external case in `lid_behind_ghost`, are not mentioned.

**Impact:** a reader would expect the frontend to guard against any enabled 0×0 output. For internal ghosts, only the `jq` filter does that. For an enabled modeless external, both outputs still count as enabled, so the real panel can still be turned off from the panel.

**Suggested change:** drop or rewrite the `parseDisplays` sentence, say "internal connector", and update the Tests paragraph to list the tests at head.

### The `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-laptop` change is not described

The PR also changes `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-laptop`, which is used by `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` (lid events, sleep and wake, the monitor watcher), `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal` ("Laptop Display") and `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror` ("Mirror Display"). Neither the title nor the description mentions it; only the last commit message hints at it. Running those scripts from both trees with every other helper stubbed:

| Case (synthetic monitor list, ghost listed first) | Before this PR | At head |
|---|---|---|
| Lid closed and docked, real `eDP-2` disabled | disables `eDP-1` (the ghost) | disables `eDP-2` |
| `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal off` with an external | disables `eDP-1`, notifies "Laptop display disabled" | disables `eDP-2` |
| `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror on` | `mirror = "eDP-1"` (mirrors the 0×0 ghost) | `mirror = "eDP-2"` |
| Lid open, ghost already disabled | `hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", mode = "preferred", ... })`, which re-enables the ghost | no call |

Without a ghost, or with the ghost listed after the real panel, both versions behave the same.

**Impact:** this is an improvement, but it changes lid, clamshell and mirror behaviour on affected laptops, which a maintainer would not expect from a Display-panel PR. The last row also matters for #10198: before this change, a lid-open sync could re-enable a ghost that #10198 had disabled. Whether the two would repeatedly toggle it on real hardware was not tested.

**Suggested change:** mention the laptop-helper change and its effect on the clamshell, laptop-display and mirror commands in the description, and consider reflecting it in the title.

**Optional test improvement:** two changes to the production filters still pass both changed test files:

- Removing the `availableModes` clause from `ghost`. That clause alone keeps a 0×0 internal connector with modes but no EDID identity (for example a DSI panel disabled since boot). A fixture with a disabled, 0×0 internal connector with empty identity and a non-empty `availableModes`, expected in line 7, would cover it.
- Filtering disabled externals out of line 7. No `omarchy-monitor-state` fixture has a disabled external. A disabled HDMI fixture expected in line 7 would cover it.

**Related open PRs:** draft #12683 carries an earlier form of this filter in `bin/omarchy-monitor-state` and `test/shell.d/monitor-state-test.sh`, without the laptop-helper or line 1 and 3 changes, so the two need deliberate reconciliation. #13293 and #11855 add `scale` to the same display-list projection, and a textual merge of this PR with #12683, #13293 or #11855 conflicts at that line.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source reading of the changed scripts, their consumers at head and on the current `quattro` tip, Hyprland 0.56.2 and aquamarine 0.15.1. Repository tests, test mutations, synthetic Hyprland-shaped monitor lists and the real clamshell, internal and mirror scripts were run in an isolated sandbox with `hyprctl` and other helpers stubbed. Nothing was tested on real hardware or a live Hyprland session: the ghost's exact output on a dual-GPU laptop and any interaction with #10198 at runtime are unverified.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
